title: std::string Basics
learningObjectives: Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: std::string manages text and its length, and supports assignment, comparison, concatenation and member operations.
understand.whyItMatters: It is a safer, easier default for ordinary text than manually managed character buffers.
understand.explain: Use size, clear and normal string operations; avoid manual terminator management.

examples.title: Initialize string
examples.explanation: string tracks length without manual termination.

examples.title: Assign and clear
examples.explanation: Assignment replaces content and clear empties it.

examples.title: Change a character
examples.explanation: Indexing modifies a character within bounds.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five std::string Basics examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating std::string basics. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.

questions.explanation: It owns and tracks its text.
